sentences.text: Globidentosuchus brachyrostris was a small crocodilian measuring approximately 1.72 meters in length and weighing about 16.7 kilograms.
It possessed a very short, robust skull where each lower jaw held 18 teeth: ten conical front teeth and eight spherical, robust rear teeth.
The tightly packed spherical teeth formed a specialized crushing unit designed to break hard-shelled prey like molluscs.
This species shared its Late Miocene wetland habitat with giant crocodilians such as Purussaurus, Mourasuchus, and Gryposuchus.
The genus Globidentosuchus was first described in 2013 by T. M. Scheyer and colleagues, with the only known species being Globidentosuchus brachyrostris.
Phylogenetic analyses often place Globidentosuchus as one of the most basal members of the Caimaninae subfamily.
Fossils are found in the Middle and Upper Members of the Urumaco Formation in Urumaco, Venezuela, dating to the late Middle to Late Miocene between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago.
Globidentosuchus inhabited the wetlands of northern Venezuela until the Late Miocene, going extinct by the Early Pliocene.

It is debated whether Globidentosuchus represents a relict population of basal caimanines that survived in Central and northern South America into the Late Miocene, a hypothesis requiring more fossil evidence to confirm.
